title: fix(gateway): prevent stale previews after broad invalidation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An older optional transcript backfill could restore stale assistant preview text after a broad invalidation cleared retained database facts. This follows up #175534.

## User Impact

Session previews retain the latest committed text when a stale optional backfill finishes after invalidation. No migration or configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing projection revision check to every backfill publication. A superseded result is discarded and the next demand can recompute it. No new generation, handshake, SQL, schema, or public API is introduced. The accepted edge case is a deferred optional preview until the next demand after invalidation; replacement/private-session authority checks remain intact.

## Evidence

Validation: the new production-boundary regression fails on the base (older text replaces the committed preview) and passes with this change. Both projection foreground/backfill files pass: 25 tests. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks pass. One independent Codex review is clean. Broad static gates and tests run in PR CI. No update cell is needed.

| Warmed-turn count | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All-thread statements, median [min–max] | 57 [57–59] | 57 [57–59] |
| Requests, median [min–max] | 16 [16–18] | 16 [16–18] |
| MAIN statements | 0 | 0 |

One matching pair on base 3ce9e7c2961c and candidate 67798fd060df confirms unchanged warmed counts (means 57.2 statements / 16.2 requests / 0 MAIN on both). No performance improvement is claimed. Both warm windows have complete causal coverage; all 13 top-level turns, RPCs, cron, compaction and shutdown passed. The same later subagent fixture failed to produce a spawn receipt in both arms, so this is warmed-turn evidence, not a full-workload pass. Area T1 calls remain 0 → 0; this change only gates publication of already-read facts. No checks were removed. Diff: 33 additions, 2 deletions across two files (production +2/−2).

Knip export scans on this exact head and base 3ce9e7c2961c report the same 14 production and 19 full-tree findings in untouched files; script exports are clean. No new findings.
